correctness.rationale: The ten disjoint Fano point-subset cases (1+7+21+7+28+28+7+21+7+1=128) show the two-step map on either shore is an idempotent projection onto 58 subsets. Its recurrent dynamics is the 58-symbol swap; exact fiber weights 36,36 and 56 ones yield all five orbit-basin classes and 16,384 total configurations. The one-step map image has 72 states per shore, establishing the sharp first-entry distribution; explicit two-point witness disproves F^3=F. A Python XOR-incidence implementation and an independent C++ explicitly-labelled graph functional-digraph algorithm exhaustively reproduced all counts, 6-cycle classification and identities, and their source/output files were replayed from the package.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General symmetric-threshold theorems imply the set of possible periods but neither the sharp identity F^4=F^2 nor the number of Heawood recurrent orbits, exact attraction weights and first-entry times. Neither source provides a stronger graph-family orbit census implying these. The Heawood graph is not a tree, clique or hypercube, and its Fano plane incidence constraints drive the result.

originality.rationale: The asserted contribution is the graph-specific Fano incidence projection, sharp two-update cutoff and full recurrence and basin census. The classical symmetric-threshold at-most-two period theorem is prior work, as are the Heawood graph and its elementary six-cycle geometry. The closest accessible complete primary works have different objectives and no implication deriving these precise finite counts; an indexed novelty search of aliases, graph structures and parameters found no equivalent. Residual risk of overlooked unindexed historical enumeration is explicitly retained.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is the unique small cubic girth-six cage and the canonical Fano plane incidence graph. Exact recurrence counts, an explicit 58-symbol conjugacy on the periodic set, a sharp global entrance bound and exact attraction distributions are natural complete dynamics invariants. The 28 Fano hexagons geometrically identify nonconstant equilibria and the two exceptional fiber weights explain concentrated basins; the result is a motivated complete finite classification rather than a routine parameter substitution or unmotivated restricted census.
